title: Learn Go
description: Learn Go by reading a focused explanation, editing real code, and checking exact output.

lessons.title: Learn Go
lessons.instruction:
Go programs begin in package main and start at the main function. The fmt package lets a program write text to standard output.

Change the program so it prints exactly:

local practice ready

lessons.title: Declaring a Variable
lessons.instruction:
A var declaration gives a value a name and a type. Replace the placeholder with a string variable named language whose value is Go, then print it.

Expected output:

Go

lessons.title: Basic Variables
lessons.instruction:
Variables can hold different kinds of values. Declare port as an int with value 8080 and secure as a bool with value true. Print both with one fmt.Println call.

Expected output:

8080 true
lessons.solution:
package main

import "fmt"

func main() {
	var port int = 8080
	var secure bool = true
	fmt.Println(port, secure)
}

lessons.title: Short Variable Declaration
lessons.instruction:
Inside a function, := declares a variable and infers its type. Declare count with :=, give it the value 3, and print it with the existing format string.

Expected output:

jobs: 3

lessons.title: Why Go?
lessons.instruction:
Go is designed around a small language, fast compilation, and straightforward deployment. Store the three words in variables and print them separated by commas.

Expected output:

simple, fast, compiled
lessons.starter:
package main

import "fmt"

func main() {
	first := "simple"
	second := "TODO"
	third := "TODO"
	fmt.Printf("%s, %s, %s\n", first, second, third)
}
lessons.solution:
package main

import "fmt"

func main() {
	first := "simple"
	second := "fast"
	third := "compiled"
	fmt.Printf("%s, %s, %s\n", first, second, third)
}

lessons.title: Comments
lessons.instruction:
A line beginning with // is ignored by the compiler. Turn the invalid English sentence into a comment so the program builds.

Expected output:

comments do not run

lessons.title: The Compilation Process
lessons.instruction:
The Go tool turns source code into a binary, then that binary can run. Replace the missing stage.

Expected output:

source -> binary -> run
lessons.starter:
package main

import "fmt"

func main() {
	source := "source"
	middle := "TODO"
	run := "run"
	fmt.Printf("%s -> %s -> %s\n", source, middle, run)
}
lessons.solution:
package main

import "fmt"

func main() {
	source := "source"
	middle := "binary"
	run := "run"
	fmt.Printf("%s -> %s -> %s\n", source, middle, run)
}

lessons.title: Fast and Compiled
lessons.instruction:
A compiled program does its translation work before it is executed. Complete the two variables.

Expected output:

compiled once, run many
lessons.starter:
package main

import "fmt"

func main() {
	builds := "TODO"
	runs := "TODO"
	fmt.Printf("compiled %s, run %s\n", builds, runs)
}
lessons.solution:
package main

import "fmt"

func main() {
	builds := "once"
	runs := "many"
	fmt.Printf("compiled %s, run %s\n", builds, runs)
}

lessons.title: Type Sizes
lessons.instruction:
An int64 always occupies 8 bytes. Pass value to unsafe.Sizeof so the program reports its size.

Expected output:

8

lessons.title: Which Type Should I Use?
lessons.instruction:
Choose types that describe the data: int for a count, float64 for a decimal ratio, and bool for a yes/no state. Fill the values without changing their declared types.

Expected output:

12 0.5 true
lessons.starter:
package main

import "fmt"

func main() {
	var requests int = 0
	var ratio float64 = 0
	var enabled bool = false
	fmt.Println(requests, ratio, enabled)
}
lessons.solution:
package main

import "fmt"

func main() {
	var requests int = 12
	var ratio float64 = 0.5
	var enabled bool = true
	fmt.Println(requests, ratio, enabled)
}

lessons.title: Go Is Statically Typed
lessons.instruction:
Once count is inferred as an int, assigning a string to it is a compile error. Fix the assignment while keeping count numeric.

Expected output:

4
lessons.starter:
package main

import "fmt"

func main() {
	count := 3
	count = "four"
	fmt.Println(count)
}
lessons.solution:
package main

import "fmt"

func main() {
	count := 3
	count = 4
	fmt.Println(count)
}

lessons.title: Compiled vs. Interpreted
lessons.instruction:
Go normally compiles source into a native executable. Replace the placeholder value.

Expected output:

Go is compiled

lessons.title: Same Line Declarations
lessons.instruction:
Go can declare multiple variables in one statement. Replace the two separate declarations with one short declaration on a single line.

Expected output:

api:8080
lessons.starter:
package main

import "fmt"

func main() {
	name := "api"
	port := 0
	fmt.Printf("%s:%d\n", name, port)
}

lessons.title: Small Memory Footprint
lessons.instruction:
A byte stores a small integer using one byte. Create a byte slice containing four values, then let len report its element count.

Expected output:

buffer bytes: 4

lessons.title: Constants
lessons.instruction: Constants name values that cannot change while the program runs. Set maxRetries to 3.

lessons.title: Computed Constants
lessons.instruction: A constant expression can be calculated from other constants at compile time. Define seconds using minutes and secondsPerMinute.
lessons.starter:
package main

import "fmt"

func main() {
	const minutes = 2
	const secondsPerMinute = 60
	const seconds = minutes
	fmt.Println(seconds)
}
lessons.solution:
package main

import "fmt"

func main() {
	const minutes = 2
	const secondsPerMinute = 60
	const seconds = minutes * secondsPerMinute
	fmt.Println(seconds)
}

lessons.title: Comparing Go's Speed
lessons.instruction: Go compiles to native machine code before execution. Correct both descriptors of its usual build model.
lessons.starter:
package main

import "fmt"

func main() {
	const translation = "interpreted"
	const target = "bytecode"
	fmt.Println(translation, target)
}
lessons.solution:
package main

import "fmt"

func main() {
	const translation = "compiled"
	const target = "native"
	fmt.Println(translation, target)
}

lessons.title: Formatting Strings in Go
lessons.instruction: Printf substitutes values into formatting verbs. Use %s for the name and %d for the task count.

lessons.title: Runes and String Encoding
lessons.instruction: len counts UTF-8 bytes, not characters. Count the runes in the string instead.

lessons.title: Fix Bugs
lessons.instruction: The total should include tax. Correct the arithmetic operator without changing the values.
lessons.starter:
package main

import "fmt"

func main() {
	price, tax := 100, 5
	total := price - tax
	fmt.Println(total)
}
lessons.solution:
package main

import "fmt"

func main() {
	price, tax := 100, 5
	total := price + tax
	fmt.Println(total)
}

lessons.title: Fix Types
lessons.instruction: Integer division discards the fractional part. Convert before dividing so the average retains its decimal value.
lessons.starter:
package main

import "fmt"

func main() {
	total := 5
	average := float64(total / 2)
	fmt.Printf("%.1f\n", average)
}
lessons.solution:
package main

import "fmt"

func main() {
	total := 5
	average := float64(total) / 2
	fmt.Printf("%.1f\n", average)
}

lessons.title: Type Inference
lessons.instruction: The := declaration infers a variable's type from its value. Make value infer as a string.

lessons.title: Format Practice
lessons.instruction: A width and leading-zero flag can pad an integer. Format id as a three-digit value.

lessons.title: Conditionals
lessons.instruction: An if branch runs only when its condition is true. Accept scores of 60 or higher.

lessons.title: The Initial Statement of an If Block
lessons.instruction: An if statement may initialize a value scoped to its branches. Compare the initialized length with the correct value.

lessons.title: Switch
lessons.instruction: A switch selects the first matching case. Correct the label for day 2.

lessons.title: Calculate Balance
lessons.instruction: Withdraw only when enough funds are available. Fix the balance calculation for this valid withdrawal.

lessons.title: Functions
lessons.instruction: Functions package reusable behavior behind a name. Make greet return the requested greeting.

lessons.title: Multiple Parameters
lessons.instruction: Parameters supply separate inputs to a function. Use both quantity and unitPrice to calculate the total.

lessons.title: Unit Test Lessons
lessons.instruction: A deterministic function is easy to test with known inputs and output. Correct add so the printed test case passes.

lessons.title: Declaration Syntax
lessons.instruction: A function declaration names its parameters before its return type. Build the label from both declared parameters.

lessons.title: Passing Variables by Value
lessons.instruction: An int parameter receives a copy, so changing it does not change the caller's variable. Increment the local copy.

lessons.title: Ignoring Return Values
lessons.instruction: Use the blank identifier when a returned value is intentionally unused. Ignore the remainder and print only the quotient.

lessons.title: Named Return Values
lessons.instruction: Named results are variables initialized to zero values. Assign width and height before the bare return.

lessons.title: The Benefits of Named Returns
lessons.instruction: Named results can clarify which of several same-typed values is returned. Assign the smaller value to min and the larger to max.

lessons.title: Explicit Returns
lessons.instruction: An explicit return states the result directly, even when the result is named. Return the square of value.

lessons.title: Early Returns
lessons.instruction: An early return handles an exceptional case before the main path. Return missing when name is empty.

lessons.title: Functions As Values
lessons.instruction: A function can be assigned to a variable and called through it. Assign add as the selected operation.

lessons.title: Anonymous Functions
lessons.instruction: An anonymous function defines behavior inline without a package-level name. Make the assigned function square its argument.

lessons.title: Defer
lessons.instruction: A deferred call runs when its surrounding function returns. Defer cleanup so it happens after work.

lessons.title: Block Scope
lessons.instruction: A variable declared inside a block can shadow an outer variable only within that block. Print the outer value after the block.

lessons.title: Processing Orders
lessons.instruction: Keep pricing logic in a function. Apply a ten-percent discount to the order amount.

lessons.title: Closures
lessons.instruction: A closure retains variables from the environment where it was created. Keep count outside the returned function so calls accumulate.

lessons.title: Currying
lessons.instruction: A curried function captures one argument and returns a function that accepts the next. Make multiplier apply multiplication.

lessons.title: Structs in Go
lessons.instruction: A struct groups named fields into one value. Initialize Ada's age correctly.

lessons.title: Nested Structs in Go
lessons.instruction: A struct field can contain another struct. Set the nested address city to Lahore.

lessons.title: Anonymous Structs in Go
lessons.instruction: An anonymous struct is useful for a small one-off value. Complete the inline point without declaring a named type.

lessons.title: Embedded Structs
lessons.instruction: Embedding promotes an inner struct's fields to the outer value. Read the promoted name field directly from member.

lessons.title: Struct Methods in Go
lessons.instruction: A method associates behavior with a receiver type. Make rectangle.area use both receiver fields.

lessons.title: Memory Layout
lessons.instruction: Field alignment can add padding to a struct. Group the byte fields after the int64 to reduce this value's size.

lessons.title: Empty Struct
lessons.instruction: struct{} carries no data, so it is a useful map value for a set. Add go to the set.

lessons.title: Empty Struct Memory
lessons.instruction: An empty struct has size zero because it stores no fields. Measure struct{} instead of an integer.

lessons.title: Update Users
lessons.instruction: Ranging over structs yields copies. Update each slice element by index so the stored user becomes active.

lessons.title: Send Message
lessons.instruction: A method can format data held by its struct receiver. Return recipient followed by the message body.

lessons.title: Interfaces in Go
lessons.instruction: An interface describes behavior through method signatures. Make dog satisfy speaker by returning the sound its Speak method promises.

lessons.title: Interface Implementation
lessons.instruction: A type implements an interface when its method set matches. Complete rectangle.Area so it can be passed to printArea as a shape.

lessons.title: Interfaces Are Implemented Implicitly
lessons.instruction: Go has no implements declaration. Give user the String method required by fmt.Stringer; the existing assignment then works automatically.

lessons.title: Interfaces Quiz
lessons.instruction: Interface satisfaction depends on exact method names and signatures. Rename Drive so car satisfies mover, then let the comma-ok assertion confirm it.

lessons.title: Multiple Interfaces
lessons.instruction: Interfaces can embed other interfaces. Use both methods exposed by readWriter to copy the source text into the device before printing it.

lessons.title: Name Your Interface Parameters
lessons.instruction: A named interface parameter can be used like any other value. Name the fmt.Stringer parameter value and return its String result.

lessons.title: Type Assertions in Go
lessons.instruction: A comma-ok type assertion safely reveals an interface's concrete value. Assert the stored value as int instead of string.
lessons.starter:
package main

import "fmt"

func main() {
	var value any = 42
	number, ok := value.(string)
	fmt.Println(number, ok)
}
lessons.solution:
package main

import "fmt"

func main() {
	var value any = 42
	number, ok := value.(int)
	fmt.Println(number, ok)
}

lessons.title: Type Switches
lessons.instruction: A type switch selects behavior using an interface's concrete type. Add the case needed to classify the int value as number.

lessons.title: Clean Interfaces
lessons.instruction: Keep interfaces as small as their consumer needs. Read Count through the one-method counter interface instead of inventing a larger contract.

lessons.title: Message Formatter
lessons.instruction: An interface lets callers use different formatting strategies. Implement markdown.Format so render can format the message without knowing the concrete type.

lessons.title: Process Notifications
lessons.instruction: A slice of interface values can hold different notifier types. Complete sms.Notify so process can dispatch both implementations uniformly.

lessons.title: The Error Interface
lessons.instruction: The error interface requires Error() string. Return the validation message so validationError behaves like a standard Go error.

lessons.title: Formatting Strings Review
lessons.instruction: Formatting verbs must match their values. Use %s for the user's name and %d for the attempt count.

lessons.title: The Error Interface
lessons.instruction: Functions return error values so callers can handle failure explicitly. Return an error when the divisor is zero.

lessons.title: Errors Quiz
lessons.instruction: Wrapped errors preserve an underlying cause. Replace direct equality with errors.Is so the sentinel is recognized through the wrapper.

lessons.title: The Errors Package
lessons.instruction: errors.New creates a simple error from a fixed message. Replace the placeholder with the failure the caller should receive.

lessons.title: Panic
lessons.instruction: Panic stops normal execution and carries a value; reserve it for unrecoverable states. Panic with the message observed by the deferred recovery.

lessons.title: User Input
lessons.instruction: fmt.Fscan parses whitespace-separated input and reports an error. Scan the provided reader into age before printing it.

lessons.title: Loops in Go
lessons.instruction: Go's for loop repeats initialization, condition, and post steps. Include 4 when summing the integers from 1 through 4.

lessons.title: Omitting Conditions from a for Loop in Go
lessons.instruction: A bare for loop repeats until control leaves it. Adjust the explicit break so the counter reaches 4.

lessons.title: There Is No While Loop in Go
lessons.instruction: Go expresses a while-style loop with for followed by one condition. Change the condition so it runs three times.

lessons.title: Fizzbuzz
lessons.instruction: FizzBuzz combines iteration with divisibility checks. Print Fizz for multiples of 3 and Buzz for multiples of 5 from 1 through 5.

lessons.title: Continue & Break
lessons.instruction: continue skips the current iteration; break leaves the loop. Skip even numbers and stop after printing 5.

lessons.title: Connections
lessons.instruction: Nested loops can visit every unique pair. Start the inner loop after the current index so four users produce six connections without duplicates or self-pairs.

lessons.title: Arrays in Go
lessons.instruction: An array has a fixed length that is part of its type. Include every element of the three-item array in the total.

lessons.title: Slices in Go
lessons.instruction: A slice expression uses an exclusive upper bound. Slice positions 1 through 3 from values.

lessons.title: Slices Review
lessons.instruction: append returns the updated slice header. Assign its result back to values so the new element is visible.

lessons.title: Make
lessons.instruction: make creates a slice with a chosen length and zero values. Allocate three slots so all indexed assignments fit.
lessons.starter:
package main

import "fmt"

func main() {
	values := make([]int, 2)
	values[0], values[1] = 4, 5
	fmt.Println(len(values))
}
lessons.solution:
package main

import "fmt"

func main() {
	values := make([]int, 3)
	values[0], values[1], values[2] = 4, 5, 6
	fmt.Println(len(values))
}

lessons.title: Len and Cap Review
lessons.instruction: len counts accessible elements; cap counts the backing capacity from the slice start. Print both values for this allocation.

lessons.title: Variadic
lessons.instruction: A variadic parameter arrives as a slice. Range over values and return their sum instead of their count.

lessons.title: Append
lessons.instruction: append may produce a new slice header and backing array. Keep its returned slice when adding rust.

lessons.title: Range
lessons.instruction: range yields an index followed by the element value. Sum the values, not their indexes.

lessons.title: Slice of Slices
lessons.instruction: A slice can contain other slices, forming rows with independent lengths. Index the second row's third value.

lessons.title: Tricky Slices
lessons.instruction: Sub-slices normally share a backing array. Copy the first two values before editing the sub-slice so original remains unchanged.

lessons.title: Message Filter
lessons.instruction: Build a filtered slice by appending only allowed words. Exclude spam while preserving the other words' order.

lessons.title: Password Strength
lessons.instruction: A useful password check combines rules. Require at least eight runes and at least one digit; this all-letter password should be weak.

lessons.title: Message Tagger
lessons.instruction: Derive a slice of tags from message content. Add failure when the message contains failed while retaining the existing urgent tag.

lessons.title: Maps
lessons.instruction: A map associates unique keys with values. Build the map so looking up "go" reports its release year.

lessons.title: Mutations
lessons.instruction: Map entries can be inserted, updated, and deleted. Update the active count and remove the obsolete key.

lessons.title: Key Types
lessons.instruction: Any comparable type can be a map key, including a struct whose fields are comparable. Look up the coordinate (2, 3).

lessons.title: Count Instances
lessons.instruction: A frequency map counts repeated values in one pass. Count every occurrence of "go" in the slice.

lessons.title: Effective Go
lessons.instruction: A map lookup's second result distinguishes a missing key from a stored zero. Use the comma-ok form to report presence.

lessons.title: Nested
lessons.instruction: Nested maps model two levels of lookup. Read the API service's production port.

lessons.title: Distinct Words
lessons.instruction: A map with empty-struct values works as a set without storing per-key data. Count the distinct words.

lessons.title: Introduction to Pointers
lessons.instruction: A pointer stores a value's address; prefixing it with * reads the value there. Print the pointed-to number.
lessons.starter:
package main

import "fmt"

func main() {
	value := 42
	pointer := &value
	fmt.Println(pointer == nil)
}
lessons.solution:
package main

import "fmt"

func main() {
	value := 42
	pointer := &value
	fmt.Println(*pointer)
}

lessons.title: References
lessons.instruction: A pointer refers to the same storage as its original variable. Assign through the pointer so both names observe 9.
lessons.starter:
package main

import "fmt"

func main() {
	count := 4
	reference := &count
	copy := *reference
	copy = 9
	fmt.Println(count)
}
lessons.solution:
package main

import "fmt"

func main() {
	count := 4
	reference := &count
	*reference = 9
	fmt.Println(count)
}

lessons.title: Pass by Reference
lessons.instruction: Go passes arguments by value, but a copied pointer still identifies the caller's value. Make swap exchange both integers.

lessons.title: Pointers Quiz
lessons.instruction: Two pointers are equal when they hold the same address. Point both variables at the same integer.
lessons.starter:
package main

import "fmt"

func main() {
	first, second := 5, 5
	a, b := &first, &second
	fmt.Println(a == b)
}
lessons.solution:
package main

import "fmt"

func main() {
	first := 5
	a, b := &first, &first
	fmt.Println(a == b)
}

lessons.title: Nil Pointers
lessons.instruction: A nil pointer has no value to dereference. Guard the access and return the supplied fallback.

lessons.title: Pointer Receivers
lessons.instruction: A method with a pointer receiver can mutate its value. Make increment persist the updated counter.

lessons.title: Pointer Receiver Code
lessons.instruction: Pointer-receiver methods can update multiple struct fields in place. Implement move so the point changes by the supplied deltas.

lessons.title: Pointer Performance
lessons.instruction: Passing a pointer avoids copying a large value when read-only access is enough. Change checksum to accept the existing buffer by pointer.

lessons.title: Update Balance
lessons.instruction: Use a pointer receiver when an operation must persist account state. Apply the deposit to the account's balance.

lessons.title: Packages
lessons.instruction: Packages group reusable declarations behind an import path. Call the imported strings package to normalize the command.

lessons.title: Package Naming
lessons.instruction: Code refers to an imported package by its declared name or an explicit alias. Use a short alias for strings and call it.

lessons.title: Install
lessons.instruction: go install builds a command and places its binary in the Go bin directory. Complete the command for a versioned tool.

lessons.title: Modules
lessons.instruction: A module identifies a collection of versioned Go packages. Complete the directive that begins a go.mod file.

lessons.title: Go Environment
lessons.instruction: go env reports configuration used by the Go toolchain. Select the variable that names the module-cache location.

lessons.title: First Local Program
lessons.instruction: An executable Go program uses package main and a main function. Make this local program print its greeting.

lessons.title: Go Run
lessons.instruction: go run compiles and immediately executes named source files. Assemble the command that runs main.go.

lessons.title: Go Build
lessons.instruction: go build compiles a package without installing it. Choose the command that creates an executable from the current module.

lessons.title: Go Install
lessons.instruction: For the current command package, go install builds and copies the executable to GOBIN. Select that local-package form.

lessons.title: Custom Package
lessons.instruction: Exported package names begin with an uppercase letter. Rename the helper so code outside its package could call it.

lessons.title: Custom Package Continued
lessons.instruction: Callers qualify an exported declaration with its package name. Model that boundary by routing main through the reusable formatter.

lessons.title: Remote Packages
lessons.instruction: Remote import paths identify the module host and package location. Normalize the path without fetching it.

lessons.title: Clean Packages
lessons.instruction: A focused package exposes a small API and keeps details private. Use the exported operation instead of duplicating its internal rule.

lessons.title: Concurrency
lessons.instruction: A goroutine runs independently; synchronization makes its result observable before main exits. Wait for the worker's message.
lessons.starter:
package main

import "fmt"

func main() {
	done := make(chan string, 1)
	go func() { done <- "worker done" }()
	fmt.Println("main done")
}
lessons.solution:
package main

import "fmt"

func main() {
	done := make(chan string, 1)
	go func() { done <- "worker done" }()
	fmt.Println(<-done)
}

lessons.title: Channels
lessons.instruction: Channels transfer typed values between goroutines. Receive the value sent by the producer instead of printing a placeholder.
lessons.starter:
package main

import "fmt"

func main() {
	values := make(chan int, 1)
	values <- 8
	fmt.Println(0)
}
lessons.solution:
package main

import "fmt"

func main() {
	values := make(chan int, 1)
	values <- 8
	fmt.Println(<-values)
}

lessons.title: Channels
lessons.instruction: Directional channel parameters document whether a function sends or receives. Give produce a send-only channel parameter and use it.

lessons.title: Buffered Channels
lessons.instruction: A buffered channel accepts values without an immediate receiver until its capacity is full. Buffer both sends, then receive their sum.
lessons.starter:
package main

import "fmt"

func main() {
	values := make(chan int, 1)
	values <- 4
	fmt.Println(<-values)
}
lessons.solution:
package main

import "fmt"

func main() {
	values := make(chan int, 2)
	values <- 4
	values <- 5
	fmt.Println(<-values + <-values)
}

lessons.title: Closing Channels in Go
lessons.instruction: Receiving from a closed, drained channel returns its zero value and false. Close the channel before the second receive.
lessons.starter:
package main

import "fmt"

func main() {
	values := make(chan int, 1)
	values <- 7
	value, ok := <-values
	fmt.Println(value, ok)
}
lessons.solution:
package main

import "fmt"

func main() {
	values := make(chan int, 1)
	values <- 7
	close(values)
	<-values
	value, ok := <-values
	fmt.Println(value, ok)
}

lessons.title: Range
lessons.instruction: Ranging over a channel receives until that channel closes. Close the populated channel and total every value.
lessons.starter:
package main

import "fmt"

func main() {
	values := make(chan int, 3)
	values <- 2
	values <- 3
	values <- 4
	close(values)
	total := 0
	for value := range values {
		total = value
	}
	fmt.Println(total)
}
lessons.solution:
package main

import "fmt"

func main() {
	values := make(chan int, 3)
	values <- 2
	values <- 3
	values <- 4
	close(values)
	total := 0
	for value := range values {
		total += value
	}
	fmt.Println(total)
}

lessons.title: Select
lessons.instruction: select waits until one channel operation can proceed. Receive the ready result and label its source.

lessons.title: Select Default Case
lessons.instruction: A default case makes select non-blocking when no communication is ready. Add the fallback behavior.

lessons.title: Channels Review
lessons.instruction: A channel pipeline connects concurrent stages while preserving type safety. Send three integers, close the input, and receive their squared total.

lessons.title: Ping Pong
lessons.instruction: Two channels can coordinate a request and response between goroutines. Send ping to the worker and print its pong reply.

lessons.title: Mutexes in Go
lessons.instruction: A mutex protects shared state so only one goroutine changes it at a time. Lock the counter around each increment.

lessons.title: Why Is It Called a 'mutex'?
lessons.instruction: Mutex means mutual exclusion: one caller enters the critical section while others wait. Guard the vault's balance update.

lessons.title: Mutex Review
lessons.instruction: Keep a mutex beside the value it protects. Complete the safe score method, including a deferred unlock.

lessons.title: RW Mutex
lessons.instruction: RWMutex separates shared reads from exclusive writes. Use a read lock while looking up the language.

lessons.title: Read/Write Mutex Review
lessons.instruction: Use RLock for cache reads and Lock for cache writes. Complete both methods without exposing the map unsafely.

lessons.title: Generics in Go
lessons.instruction: Type parameters let one function work safely with many element types. Return the first value from any non-empty slice.

lessons.title: Why Generics?
lessons.instruction: Generics remove duplicated algorithms while preserving concrete types. Complete one sum function that accepts integers or floats.

lessons.title: Constraints
lessons.instruction: A constraint defines the operations allowed for a type parameter. Permit integer-like types, then double the input.

lessons.title: Interface Type Lists
lessons.instruction: A type list forms a union of permitted underlying types. Complete abs for values based on int or int64.

lessons.title: Parametric Constraints
lessons.instruction: Method constraints require each type argument to provide specific behavior. Render any value implementing fmt.Stringer.

lessons.title: Naming Generic Types
lessons.instruction: Short type-parameter names suit small scopes; descriptive names help longer declarations. Complete the reusable Stack[T] methods.

lessons.title: Lack of Enums
lessons.instruction: Go models enum-like values with a named type and constants. Select the running status instead of an untyped number.

lessons.title: Type Definitions
lessons.instruction: A type definition creates a distinct type, preventing accidental mixing. Convert Celsius to Fahrenheit explicitly.

lessons.title: Iota
lessons.instruction: Within a const block, iota advances from zero. Use bit shifts to give each permission its own flag.

lessons.title: Go Proverbs
lessons.instruction: Go proverbs express design guidance, not compiler rules. Complete the proverb that favors readable code over ingenuity.
